title: History of Measles
snippet:
measles virus

## Pre-vaccine era

Francis Home, a Scottish physician, demonstrated in 1757 that measles is caused by an infectious agent in the blood of patients.

In 1912, measles became a nationally notifiable disease in the United States, requiring U.S. healthcare providers and laboratories to report all diagnosed cases. In the first decade of reporting, an average of 6,000 measles-related deaths were reported each year. [...] In 1963, John Enders and colleagues transformed their Edmonston-B strain of measles virus into a vaccine and licensed it in the United States. In 1968, an improved and even weaker measles vaccine, developed by Maurice Hilleman and colleagues, began to be distributed. This vaccine, called the Edmonston-Enders (formerly "Moraten") strain has been the only measles vaccine used in the United States since 1968. [...] In 1954, John F. Enders and Dr. Thomas C. Peebles collected blood samples from several ill students during a measles outbreak in Boston, Massachusetts. They wanted to isolate the measles virus in the student's blood and create a measles vaccine. They succeeded in isolating measles in 13-year-old David Edmonston's blood.

title: US Measles Total Tops 2,300 — The Most in 35 Years
snippet:
Confirmed measles cases in the United States in 2026 have reached 2,318, surpassing the 2025’s total of 2,289 cases in less than 8 months. The 2026 total is the most in 35 years, since 9,643 cases were reported in 1991.

### Historical Data

The 2026 total now surpasses 2025 as the eighth worst in US history since 1985.

2026 currently sits just 504 cases behind 1985 for the seventh most cases, with current reporting rates suggesting it will surpass that number before end of year. [...] There have been 30 new outbreaks reported in 2026, and 93% of confirmed cases (1,929 of 2,073) are outbreak-associated, according to the CDC.

The 2026 total is approaching 2025’s total of 2,288 confirmed infections, which was the most US cases in 34 years (1991).

The majority of 2026 cases have occurred in South Carolina, which declared its state outbreak “ended” on April 27, 2026 with 997 infections, 21 hospitalizations, and zero related deaths. [...] The measles virus was declared “eliminated” in the United States in the year 2000.

### 2026 Data

According July 23 data from the CDC, 2,302 measles cases have been reported in 44 states plus 16 cases reported among international visitors to the United States.

The agency reports that there have been 35 new outbreaks reported in 2026, and 93% of confirmed cases (2,153 of 2,318) are outbreak-associated.
